title: —Of the offence to me, Stephen answered.
html_source:
What does Stephen mean by this, and why is it coming out now? On the simplest level, Stephen is perhaps as offended by Mulligan referring to him as

“only Dedalus”
as he is about his mother being
“beastly dead.”
Further, if Mulligan respected Stephen, or saw him as a social equal, he wouldn’t have said that. It’s another small detail that shows you how Mulligan’s interest in Stephen is insincere. I think Stephen also is offended because his mother’s death is such a huge presence in his present life–he might like to escape his fixation on it, but as we’ve already seen, the experience still haunts him.

#On a Deeper Level

Stephen is also showing Mulligan that he is unmoved by the verbal assault he was attacked with; that he has no intent of dropping his grudge. Stephen knows that behind Mulligan’s bluster is a strong desire to be adored and respected.
